_doc: The application evaluator runs each case as a baseline/no-skill arm and a with-skill arm, then grades behavior against expected_flags, expected_fix_hints, absent_signals, and the per-case criteria checklist.
subject: Use when you need to explain how parts of a system, feature, concept, page, workflow, or problem connect; identify the…

cases.scenario: A user asks: "what is the most important part of this dashboard, and how do the surrounding widgets relate to it?"
cases.context: The agent has access to the semantic-center skill and must decide whether to use it, apply its procedure, and stay inside its boundaries.
cases.question: What should the agent do, and why is semantic-center the right skill to apply?
expected_flags: Recognizes semantic-center as applicable to this request
Uses the skill-specific purpose or mental model instead of generic advice
Names the relevant boundary against intent-recognition, diagnosis, knowledge-modeling
Turns the request into concrete steps, checks, or decisions from the skill
expected_fix_hints: Apply the semantic-center workflow to the concrete scenario
State the next action and the evidence or verification needed
Call out any adjacent skill that should own a different part of the request
absent_signals: Does not answer with generic advice that could ignore semantic-center
Does not route to intent-recognition, diagnosis, knowledge-modeling when the semantic-center scope is the owner
Does not invent certification, freshness, or runtime success claims without evidence
